To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the hyperfine field of $^{254}$Es in iron is $|{B}_{{\mathrm{hf}}}({}^{254}$Es$\underline{\mathrm{F}}{\mathrm{e}}|) = 396(32)$ T and the nuclear magnetic moment of $|\mu| = 4.35(4)$ μB, where the uncertainty is one standard deviation.
we have determined the magnetic moment of einsteinium-254, and we have measured the hyperfine interaction of einsteinium impurities in an Fe host lattice.
we determined the hyperfine field of the einsteinium impurity in iron and used this information to extract the magnetic moment of the $^{254}\ensuremath{\mathrm{Es}}$ isotope.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the determination of nuclear magnetic moments of heavy nuclei.
the study of nuclear magnetic moments, nuclear spin, and hyperfine fields in actinide elements.
the study of the magnetic hyperfine interaction of actinides in an iron host.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the magnetic moment of einsteinium is 4.4(2) ${\ensuremath{\mu}N}$, where the error is a weighted average of all the previous measurements and the present work.
the magnetic moment of einsteinium is in the range of $4.0\ensuremath{\mu} _{N} \leq |\ensuremath{\mu}_{\ensuremath{\mathrm{Es}}}| \leq 4.5\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mu}_N}$.
the magnetic moment of the $^{254}\ensuremath{\mathrm{Es}}$ ground state has been measured for the first time with a precision of 9.5%.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the magnetic moments of $^{253}\mathrm{Es},^{254}\mathrm{\ensuremath{\mathit{Es}}}$, and $|{B}_\ensuremath{\mathbf{hf}}(\text{Es}\text{\textunderscore Fe})|$ were measured.
we have determined the magnetic moment of the first isotope with odd number of protons, neutrons, and fermions, $^{254}\ensuremath{\mathrm{Es}}$, in the actinide series.

the magnetic moments of $^{250}\ensuremath{\mathrm{Bk}},$ $^{253,255}\ensuremath{\text{Es}},$ and $^{255,256}\ensuremath{\mathit{Fm}}$ are now known, whereas the hyperfine fields of berkelium and californium in iron have also been measured.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the hyperfine field of the einsteinium impurities in iron is much smaller in magnitude than that of other actinides.
the magnetic moment of einsteinium is very similar to the magnetic moment of americium.
the magnetic moment of the odd-proton $1{h}_{9/2}$ orbital in $^{254}\rm{Es}$ is much smaller than the value expected from the systematics of the $N=157$ isotones.
